correctness.rationale: A four-arc in PG(2,3) uniquely specifies a smooth F_3-conic: the pencil through a rational four-frame has four members, three split pairings and one smooth member. The primary verifier exhausts all 715 four-subsets, 234 arcs, 27,261 unordered pairs and 13 lines; generates the entire PGL3(F3) of size 5,616; and enumerates exact orbit sizes 702, 936, 5,616, 1,404, 2,808, plus complement and decomposition counts. A separate coefficient sweep classifies all scalar-normalized quadrics by exact Hessian determinant and independently recovers each global count. The actual executable files and captured outputs are embedded. Finite completeness and geometric smoothness are proved; no finite-extension heuristic is used.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns projective equivalence and smooth-conic decomposition multiplicities of blocking PAIRS, not classification of individual minimal blocking sets or existence of nonblocking pencils. The 2023 finite-field pencil paper and 2025/2026 conic-union paper have different quantified conclusions. The 2022 small-plane blocking-set classification can dominate the six-point point-set count, which is expressly acknowledged as old, but it does not visibly settle the three/four algebraic conic decompositions or the five conic-pair orbits. Relevant full text and actual record searches were compared. Residual priority risk from the inaccessible 2022 full text and unindexed prior conic-pair tables remains.
residual_risks: Coolsaet et al. 2022 full text could contain or imply some six-point smooth-conic decompositions; direct full comparison was unavailable.
An unindexed historical projective classification of conic pairs over F3 might imply the five orbit counts.
The 2025/2026 union-of-curves paper was inspected for its main conic theorems but not line-by-line throughout; no claim of comprehensive full-text negative evidence is made.

value.rationale: Pairs of geometrically smooth conics are the smallest natural algebraic building blocks of nontrivial blocking unions over F3, motivated by modern work on algebraic-curve constructions. The complete five-orbit census separates trivial line-containing unions from genuine blocking sets; the exact three/four decomposition multiplicities and complement duality reveal how the extremal rational configurations are realized by conics. These intrinsic incidence invariants are not determined by the prior count of individual minimal blocking sets or by smooth-pencil existence theorems and can be used to benchmark constructive blocking-family methods.
